title: Latency-budgeted pinwheel routing and staged load-shedding policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Production observed periodic cross-region latency blasts during peak windows where requests routed by proximity caused overloaded regional GPUs and cascading retries. We need a routing policy that honors per-customer latency SLOs (p95/p99 budgets), preserves locality where possible, and gracefully sheds load when regional capacity is exhausted. Goal: Implement a topology-aware routing strategy ('pinwheel') that enforces latency budgets per request class, uses capacity signals to avoid saturating regions, and applies staged load-shedding + circuit-breakers to keep overall platform SLOs healthy.
design_summary: Pinwheel idea: each request carries a latency budget (derived from route SLO and user tier). The router attempts local dispatch first, but uses a probabilistic pin/bleed factor to occasionally route to secondary regions for cache warming and capacity smoothing. Capacity-aware steering: regions publish three signals (available worker slots, short-term queue depth, and recent tail latency) into a routing score. Circuit guards: per-region circuit state machine (CLOSED, SOFT_TRIP, HARD_TRIP) with hysteresis and token-based admission. Load-shedding tiers: Tier 0 (system-critical) never shed; Tier 1 (paid) soft-shed with queue delay + model-variant fallback; Tier 2 (best-effort) subject to hard reject when region is over threshold. The router integrates with autoscaling hints and a centralized policy store to allow emergency overrides.
acceptance_criteria: Router enforces per-request latency budget and rejects/reroutes requests predicted to exceed SLO more than 95% of the time
Regional circuit guard triggers when p99 latency > 4x target for 2 consecutive 1m windows or when available slots < 10% for >30s
Load-shedding behavior conforms to tier policies: paid customers receive model-variant fallback before hard reject
End-to-end integration tests show <5% increase in global p99 after canary rollout under synthetic regional overload
Dashboards and alerts available for routing score, circuit state transitions, shed rate by tier
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decision: use probabilistic pinwheel instead of strict geo-pinning to avoid long-term hotspots. Tradeoff: slight increase in cross-region traffic vs improved capacity smoothing.

Decision: tokenized admission limit per-region instead of global token bucket to reduce tail amplification during regional failures. Tradeoff: complexity in token reconciliation during region re-joins.
Decision: prefer model-variant fallback over immediate rejection for paid tiers to preserve UX; tradeoff is additional inference cost and potential quality variance.
Considered: fully synchronous hedging (send to two regions) but rejected due to 2x cost for steady-state traffic; instead implement selective hedging for requests with large remaining budgets.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Scoping and metrics analysis completed. Identified p99 tail coupling to queue depth and cold KV cache misses in overfilled regions.
2026-03-05: Prototype router component implemented with routing score calculation and tokenized admission. Basic state machine for circuits in place.
2026-03-08: Unit tests added for circuit transitions and token accounting. Integration tests against staging runtime show expected trip behavior under synthetic load.
2026-03-12: Load test (k6) on staging: simulated region overload; pinwheel reduced peak p99 by ~18% vs baseline geo-stickiness. Observed increased cross-region egress by 6%.
2026-03-14: Design review scheduled with Reliability and Product to confirm tiered-shedding semantics and cost impact. Blocking: final approval of model-variant fallback list from ML infra.
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated: rollout in three phases (canary 1% internal->canary 10% staging->production 1%->ramp to 20%)
Canary criteria: no >5% regression in global p50/p95/p99, shed rate <0.1% for paid tiers, no unexpected circuit flapping for >5m
Observability check: automated synthetic transactions from multiple regions every 30s exercising primary+fallback paths
Auto-rollback: if global p99 regresses by >10% or shed rate for paid tiers exceeds threshold, rollback to strict geo-pin policy via feature flag
testing_plan: Unit tests for routing score math, token allocation, and circuit state transitions
Integration in staging using a multi-region runtime cluster; inject queue-pressure and slow-worker faults
Load tests: progressive overload scenarios (10%/25%/50% extra traffic) to validate shedding thresholds and cost impact
Chaos tests: kill regional control-plane processes and validate graceful drain and re-join semantics
Quality tests: A/B evals to ensure model-variant fallback doesn't cause unacceptable regression in top-line quality metrics for paid customers
monitoring_and_runbook: Dashboards: routing_score by region, circuit_state timeline, shed_rate by customer tier, cross-region egress by route
Alerts: circuit_hard_trip (P0), shed_rate_paid_tier > 0.5% for 5m (P1), cross-region_egress_growth > 20% vs baseline (P2)

Operator actions: soft-trip remediation (reduce incoming traffic via rate-limiter, scale up regional pool, warm caches), hard-trip remediation (drain region and suspend new admissions), emergency global fallback to low-cost model pool
open_risks: Risk: increased cross-region egress could materially raise cost; mitigation: throttle pinwheel probability based on egress budget and implement egress-aware scoring
Risk: token reconciliation on region re-join may allow transient spike; mitigation: conservative token warmup and backoff windows
Risk: model-variant fallbacks may produce customer-visible quality variance; mitigation: narrow fallback list and post-deploy quality monitoring with automatic rollback triggers
notes_for_reviewers: Please evaluate the circuit thresholds (currently p99 > 4x target for 2m). Are these too aggressive for enterprise customers?
Feedback needed on token bucket reconciliation approach during region re-join — see design doc section 3.2
Confirm list of model variants approved for paid-tier fallback (ping ML infra owners)
